title: Kth Smallest Instructions
summary: Given a destination coordinate and an integer k, return the k^th lexicographically smallest sequence of 'H' (horizontal) and 'V' (vertical) moves that will lead Bob from (0,0) to the destination.
statement: Given a destination coordinate and an integer k, return the k^th lexicographically smallest sequence of 'H' (horizontal) and 'V' (vertical) moves that will lead Bob from (0,0) to the destination. Each move is either right or down, and the sequence is determined by the lexicographical order of the instruction strings.
constraints: Destination gives 1–15 vertical and horizontal moves; k is within the number of paths.
H is lexicographically before V. Return the one-indexed kth path string.
hints: At any prefix, count paths beginning with H before choosing the next character.
The H block contains C(remaining-1,vertical) paths.
If k is inside that block, append H; otherwise append V and subtract the whole H block.
All H-prefixed paths precede every V-prefixed path, so repeated block selection identifies the kth string.
editorial: All H-prefixed paths precede every V-prefixed path, so repeated block selection identifies the kth string.

tests.explanation: The first path places all three H moves before both V moves: HHHVV.
Skipping the first two H-leading combinations at the deciding prefix produces HHVVH.
